The construction on the cube, read along the rows. (a) Degree two can leave two cycles. (b) The dual octahedron, with the cube in grey and black triangles shaded; the grey collar represents the outer black triangle. Its hollow corners are $0,1,2$, and $e_0=\{0,1\}$. (c) A state, shown by solid wedges, and its opposite sides, dashed. (d) The avoided edges form a spanning tree, and the dash-dotted tree joins the white triangles, with black nodes suppressed; the ring marks its root. (e) One bold side per triangle, and the Hamiltonian cycle crossing all other sides. Disks and squares distinguish the two trees of bold edges. (f) Two states, outlined and solid, and the arrows between their chosen corners.

The example triangulation $\T$, its $13$ vertices labelled, with $G$ in grey: each vertex of $G$ sits in a face of $\T$ and each edge of $G$ crosses one edge of $\T$. Black faces are shaded. The outer face $t_0=\{0,4,5\}$ is black too, as the grey collar shows; the vertex of $G$ inside it is drawn below the disk. Its corners $0,4,5$ are hollow, and the prescribed side $e_0=\{0,4\}$ is the bottom arc. There are $11$ black faces, $11$ white faces and $33$ edges.

One black triangle $t\in A$. A state chooses the corner $s(t)$ (solid wedge). A selection built from $s$ uses one of the two bold sides at $s(t)$, and the dashed side opposite $s(t)$ is the edge of $Q_s$ in $t$.

The opposite sides (dashed) of the two states of Example~\ref{ex:states}; solid wedges mark the chosen corners and hollow circles the roots. (a) $Q_\alpha$ contains the triangle on $1,8,9$ around a white face, and its component has no root. (b) $Q_\beta$ is a forest with three components, one through each root. The proof needs a state that looks like (b).

The selection $P_\beta$ (bold). (a) The dash-dotted tree is $Y_\beta$ with its black nodes suppressed: a tree on the white faces rooted at the ringed face $y_0$ across $e_0=\{0,4\}$. The root selects $e_0$, and every other white face selects the side towards its parent. Every face has one bold side. (b) The bold edges form two trees, on the disks and on the squares, and the curve that crosses each other edge once is the Hamiltonian cycle of $G$ through all $22$ faces.

The disk identity on the $7$-cycle $1,2,3,9,10,11,6$, whose arrows leave the corners chosen by the state $\beta$ of Example~\ref{ex:states} (outlined wedges); it is the long cycle of Figure~\ref{fig:pair}. The tinted disk has $B=5$ black and $W=6$ white faces, $I=3$ vertices strictly inside (ringed: $7,8,12$) and $h=7$ edges, of which $\ell=2$ have their black face inside (marked). Each black face inside holds one outlined wedge, at a ringed vertex or at the tail of a marked arrow, which is the count $B=I+\ell$. So $W=B+1$ and $h=2\ell+3$, equivalently $2\ell-h=-3$.

A pair in a black triangle. Outlined wedges mark the first state $r(t)$; solid wedges mark the second, $s(t)$. The solid arrow belongs to $D(r,s)$, defined below. The dashed arrow orients $Q_s$ from $r(t)$ to the third corner $u(t)$, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:partner}.

The pair $(\beta,\alpha)$ of Example~\ref{ex:states}: outlined wedges mark $\beta$, solid wedges $\alpha$. The arrows $\beta(t)\to\alpha(t)$ form $D(\beta,\alpha)$, a counterclockwise cycle of length $7$ through $6,1,2,3,9,10,11$ and a clockwise triangle through $8,7,12$.
The two reversals of Lemma~\ref{lem:reversals}. The sign is that of Lemma~\ref{lem:sign}.

Cancellation in the example ($n=10$), enlarged around the three affected black faces; the rest of the triangulation is omitted. (a) The pair $(\beta,\alpha)$. Dashed edges are $Q_\alpha$; its cycle $1,8,9$ (heavy, around the tinted white face) is directed by $\beta$ from the outlined corner to the third corner. (b) Reversing that cycle moves the outlined wedges in its three faces to their third corners and leaves the solid wedges, the state $\alpha$, unchanged. Three local signs flip, so $\eps$ changes sign and the two pairs cancel in any sum weighted by a function of the second state.

A height in the example. The white face $y=\{1,8,9\}$ (tinted) and its path of faces to the outer face (dash-dotted): $y$, $\{1,7,8\}$, $\{1,6,7\}$, $\{0,1,6\}$, $\{0,5,6\}$, $t_0$. In each black face on the path the path turns around one corner; the circled sign is $+$ if that corner lies on its left and $-$ if on its right. The height of a state at $y$ adds the signs at turned corners that carry its wedge. (a) A pair whose $7$-cycle runs clockwise. Its second state $s$ has its wedge at the turned corner $6$ of $\{0,1,6\}$ and not at the turned corner $1$ of $\{1,7,8\}$, so $\eta_s(y)=-1$. (b) Reversing the $7$-cycle as in Lemma~\ref{lem:height} gives the pair $(\beta,\alpha)$ of Figure~\ref{fig:pair}, where it runs counterclockwise. The wedge in $\{0,1,6\}$ has moved to $1$, and $\eta_\alpha(y)=0$, one more, because $y$ lies inside the $7$-cycle.
The eight pairs of the example. Reversing the $7$-cycle from clockwise to counterclockwise raises $\omega$ by $L=6$ or $3$, reversing the triangle raises it by $1$, and each reversal flips $\eps$.

Two groupings of Table~\ref{tab:pairs}. Each row fixes the undirected $D$ and lists its four orientations, the $7$-cycle first; its signed second moment is $2L_1L_2$. The shaded pairs share $s=\alpha$ and cancel. The remaining pairs have six distinct good second states.

The flow network for the example. Each vertex of $X$ receives at most $2$ from the source, each incidence (thin) carries at most $1$, and each black triangle of $A$ sends at most $2$ to the sink. An integral flow of value $2|X|=20$ uses two incidences at every vertex and every triangle, the double and the solid ones, which alternate along cycles and split into the states $\beta$ and $\alpha$. Here \eqref{eq:hall} holds with equality for $S=\{2\}$, a vertex in only two black triangles.

Gluing across the separating triangle $\{3,4,5\}$ of an octahedron with a second octahedron inside one face ($9$ vertices). (a) The outer piece, cap tinted; its acyclic selection (bold) puts $3$ and $5$ in one tree. (b) The inner piece with the cap as outer face and $\{3,5\}$ prescribed. (c) The union is an acyclic selection of the whole triangulation; its trees meet those of the pieces in the edge $\{3,5\}$ or in the vertex $4$. Disks and squares mark the two trees.
